rule.missing: The runtime the category or mechanic needs is absent (tools/parity/rules.json declares the files or code markers).
rule.partial: The runtime exists but the entry has an open issue: a validation error on its record, a placeholder value, a missing item definition, an unresolved value that is not a source-data gap, a failing tagged check, or (a canonical-verification row) shipped data not yet in the state the row describes (tools/parity/rules.json requires: the tests prove the validator rule, not the data).
rule.implemented: Runtime present, data valid, every unresolved value a documented source-data gap, but no passing check tagged with the key.
rule.verified: As implemented, plus at least one passing check tagged with the key (or an accepted parent key or alias) and no failing one, in the evidence given. Quests, objectives and rewards need a passing playtest (real-game) check; quest chains follow their own rule (chains, below); the clean-character playthrough rows need one from a clean run (a passing report, strict mode ok, no console or api step in the report, and the departure boundary reached: its final boundary check passed and no PLAYTHROUGH_STOP flag); a drop probability is verified only when its sources resolve.
rule.chains: A quest chain (chain:<first quest>) is derived from its member quests: missing when a member is missing, partial when a member is partial or a check tagged with the chain key fails, verified only when every member quest is verified (each by its own real-game checks) and at least one passing real-game check is tagged with the chain key: a link of the chain, the quest runner's "<quest>: its follow-up <next> (...) is available" check made right after the predecessor was completed through play (tools/parity/rules.json playtest_tags give the chain key); otherwise implemented.
rule.source_data_gap: The sources were read and do not give a value the entry needs (the KuroDB page has no chance for a member, no meso amount, no MeowDB rule for a mechanic): the entry is excused from the exit criterion.
rule.pending_source_read: A source publishes a value the entry needs on a page that has not been read yet (for example a KuroDB item page that settles a candidate drop row, or a MeowDB item page only the item API of which was captured). Unlike a source-data gap it is not excused: the entry stays partial and counts as open for the exit criterion until the page is read and the data updated. tools/parity/rules.json pending_source_reads names the read for each; a drop record's pending_kuro_candidates row (a KuroDB row that may be the member, waiting for a read of its item page) makes its member pending even when undeclared.
rule.in_scope: false for content outside Iteration Three (rules.json out_of_scope).
rule.evidence: A unit test declares the keys it proves in its file's parity_keys(); a playtest check carries them in report.json (checks[].parity), or tools/parity/rules.json playtest_tags gives them to the checks of a scenario whose names match a pattern (hand-reviewed: only checks that prove the key). A soft check is never evidence.
